newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on improved Midwest weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on improved Midwest weather.

text.p: Improved crop seeding weather in the U.S. Midwest pressed CBOT corn futures to a lower close, traders said.
They said generally warmer, drier weather late last week and over the weekend allowed farmers to make rapid progress in seeding corn.
"U.S. weather is extremely favorable, we're making rapid planting progress," said Dale Gustafson, Smith Barney grain analyst.
The market was expecting USDA to reveal a seeding pace as of Sunday at 20 to 25 percent complete.
A week ago the corn planting pace stood at seven percent complete in the U.S. which was equal to the five-year average seeding rate.

Pressure also came from USDA's weekly export inspections report which showed corn inspections for the week ended April 24 at 30.301 million bushels, near the low end of expectations for 29 million to 35 million bushels.
But declines in futures were curbed by slow farmer selling and firm cash basis markets, traders said.
Corn ended 2-1/4 to 5-1/4 cents a bushel lower, with May down 3-3/4 at $2.90-3/4. Dec ended down four at $2.74-1/2.

Traders said the key play in the corn pit was a fund-related spread into the soybean pit. FIMAT Futures bought at least 30 million bushels of December corn and sold at least 15 million bushels of November soybeans, traders said.

In other spread trading, Continental Grain did five million bushels of May/July at even money, Farmers Commodities Corp did two million May/July at even money to 1/4 cent, premium May and LIT America spread two million July/December at 17-1/4 cents, premium July, traders said.
Lee B. Stern and Co sold seven million bushels of July and Term Commodities bought 2.5 million bushels of July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 80,000 contracts, below the 85,114 traded Friday.

In corn options, Rosenthal Collins sold 400 July $2.90 puts at nine cents, USA Trading bought 500 July $2.60 puts at 1-1/8 cents and Smith Barney bought 400 July $3.10 calls at 4-3/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, above the 17,720 traded Friday.
